}## Expand description

Used by hosts to limit resource consumption of instances.

Resources limited via this trait are primarily related to memory.

Note that this trait does not limit 100% of memory allocated. Implementers might still allocate memory to track data structures and additionally embedder-specific memory allocations are not tracked via this trait.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasmi_core/limiter.rs.html#110-115)#### fn [memory_growing](https://docs.rs#tymethod.memory_growing)(
    &mut self,
    current: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    desired: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    maximum: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [LimiterError](https://docs.rs/enum.LimiterError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasmi_core/limiter.rs.html#110-115)

#### fn [memory_growing](https://docs.rs#tymethod.memory_growing)(
    &mut self,
    current: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    desired: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    maximum: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [LimiterError](https://docs.rs/enum.LimiterError.html)>

Notifies the resource limiter that an instance’s linear memory has been requested to grow.

- `current`is the current size of the linear memory in bytes.
- `desired`is the desired size of the linear memory in bytes.
- `maximum`is either the linear memory’s maximum or a maximum from an instance allocator, also in bytes. A value of- `None`indicates that the linear memory is unbounded.

The `current` and `desired` amounts are guaranteed to always be
multiples of the WebAssembly page size, 64KiB.

[§](https://docs.rs#return-value)Return Value

If `Ok(true)` is returned from this function then the growth operation
is allowed. This means that the wasm `memory.grow` or `table.grow` instructions
will return with the `desired` size, in wasm pages. Note that even if
`Ok(true)` is returned, though, if `desired` exceeds `maximum` then the
growth operation will still fail.

If `Ok(false)` is returned then this will cause the `grow` instruction
in a module to return -1 (failure), or in the case of an embedder API
calling any of the below methods an error will be returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

If `Err(e)` is returned then the `memory.grow` or `table.grow` functions
will behave as if a trap has been raised. Note that this is not necessarily
compliant with the WebAssembly specification but it can be a handy and
useful tool to get a precise backtrace at “what requested so much memory
to cause a growth failure?”.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasmi_core/limiter.rs.html#129-134)#### fn [table_growing](https://docs.rs#tymethod.table_growing)(
    &mut self,
    current: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    desired: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    maximum: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [LimiterError](https://docs.rs/enum.LimiterError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasmi_core/limiter.rs.html#129-134)

#### fn [table_growing](https://docs.rs#tymethod.table_growing)(
    &mut self,
    current: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    desired: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    maximum: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [LimiterError](https://docs.rs/enum.LimiterError.html)>

Notifies the resource limiter that an instance’s table has been requested to grow.

- `current`is the current number of elements in the table.
- `desired`is the desired number of elements in the table.
- `maximum`is either the table’s maximum or a maximum from an instance allocator. A value of- `None`indicates that the table is unbounded.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-1)Errors

See the details on the return values for [ ResourceLimiter::memory_growing](https://docs.rs/trait.ResourceLimiter.html#tymethod.memory_growing)
for what the return values of this function indicates.

The maximum number of instances that can be created for a Wasm store.

Module instantiation will fail if this limit is exceeded.

# Trap in wasmi_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasmi_core/1.1.0/wasmi_core/struct.Trap.html

`pub struct Trap { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Error type which can be returned by Wasm code or by the host environment.

Under some conditions, Wasm execution may produce a [ Trap](https://docs.rs/struct.Trap.html),
which immediately aborts execution.
Traps cannot be handled by WebAssembly code, but are reported to the
host embedder.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a new `Trap` representing an explicit program exit with a classic `i32`
exit status value.

# UntypedVal in wasmi_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasmi_core/1.1.0/wasmi_core/struct.UntypedVal.html

# Struct UntypedVal

[Source](../src/wasmi_core/untyped.rs.html#15-28) `pub struct UntypedVal {  }`

## Expand description

An untyped value.

Provides a dense and simple interface to all functional Wasm operations.

Creates an `UntypedVal`

This sets the high 64-bits to zero if any.

Returns the underlying lower 64-bits of the `UntypedVal`

This ignores the high 64-bits of the `UntypedVal`

Decodes the slice of `UntypedVal``T`.

[§](#note)Note

`T` can either be a single type or a tuple of types depending
on the length of the `slice`.

[§](#errors)Errors

If the tuple length of `T` and the length of `slice` does not match.

Encodes the slice of `UntypedVal``T`.

[§](#note-1)Note

`T` can either be a single type or a tuple of types depending
on the length of the `slice`.

[§](#errors-1)Errors

If the tuple length of `T` and the length of `slice` does not match.

Performs copy-assignment from

`source`.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#method.clone_from)

Formats the value using the given formatter.

#[non_exhaustive]pub enum GlobalError {
    ImmutableWrite,

## Expand description

An error that may occur upon operating on global variables.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ImmutableWrite)

### ImmutableWrite

Occurs when trying to write to an immutable global variable.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.TypeMismatch)

### TypeMismatch

Occurs when trying writing a value with mismatching type to a global variable.

pub enum MemoryError {
    OutOfSystemMemory,
    OutOfBoundsGrowth,

[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html),
    },
}## Expand description

An error that may occur upon operating with virtual or linear memory.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.OutOfSystemMemory)

### OutOfSystemMemory

Tried to allocate more virtual memory than technically possible.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.OutOfBoundsGrowth)

### OutOfBoundsGrowth

Tried to grow linear memory out of its set bounds.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.OutOfBoundsAccess)

### OutOfBoundsAccess

Tried to access linear memory out of bounds.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidMemoryType)

### InvalidMemoryType

Tried to create an invalid linear memory type.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidStaticBufferSize)

### InvalidStaticBufferSize

Tried to create memory with invalid static buffer size

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ResourceLimiterDeniedAllocation)

### ResourceLimiterDeniedAllocation

If a resource limiter denied allocation or growth of a linear memory.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MinimumSizeOverflow)

### MinimumSizeOverflow

The minimum size of the memory type overflows the system index type.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MaximumSizeOverflow)

### MaximumSizeOverflow

The maximum size of the memory type overflows the system index type.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.OutOfFuel)

### OutOfFuel

Encountered if a `memory.grow` operation runs out of fuel.

# TrapCode in wasmi_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasmi_core/1.1.0/wasmi_core/enum.TrapCode.html

```
#[repr(u8)]pub enum TrapCode {
    UnreachableCodeReached = 0,
    MemoryOutOfBounds = 1,
    TableOutOfBounds = 2,
    IndirectCallToNull = 3,
    IntegerDivisionByZero = 4,
    IntegerOverflow = 5,
    BadConversionToInteger = 6,
    StackOverflow = 7,
    BadSignature = 8,
    OutOfFuel = 9,
    GrowthOperationLimited = 10,
}
```
## Expand description

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UnreachableCodeReached)

### UnreachableCodeReached = 0

Wasm code executed `unreachable` opcode.

This indicates that unreachable Wasm code was actually reached.
This opcode have a similar purpose as `ud2` in x86.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MemoryOutOfBounds)

### MemoryOutOfBounds = 1

Attempt to load or store at the address which lies outside of bounds of the memory.

Since addresses are interpreted as unsigned integers, out of bounds access can’t happen with negative addresses (i.e. they will always wrap).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.TableOutOfBounds)

### TableOutOfBounds = 2

Attempt to access table element at index which lies outside of bounds.

This typically can happen when `call_indirect` is executed
with index that lies out of bounds.

Since indexes are interpreted as unsigned integers, out of bounds access can’t happen with negative indexes (i.e. they will always wrap).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.IndirectCallToNull)

### IndirectCallToNull = 3

Indicates that a `call_indirect` instruction called a function at
an uninitialized (i.e. `null`) table index.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.IntegerDivisionByZero)

### IntegerDivisionByZero = 4

Attempt to divide by zero.

This trap typically can happen if `div` or `rem` is executed with
zero as divider.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.IntegerOverflow)

### IntegerOverflow = 5

An integer arithmetic operation caused an overflow.

This can happen when trying to do signed division (or get the remainder)
-2N-1 over -1. This is because the result +2N-1
isn’t representable as a N-bit signed integer.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BadConversionToInteger)

### BadConversionToInteger = 6

Attempted to make an invalid conversion to an integer type.

This can for example happen when trying to truncate NaNs, infinity, or value for which the result is out of range into an integer.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.StackOverflow)

### StackOverflow = 7

Stack overflow.

This is likely caused by some infinite or very deep recursion. Extensive inlining might also be the cause of stack overflow.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BadSignature)

### BadSignature = 8

Attempt to invoke a function with mismatching signature.

This can happen with indirect calls as they always specify the expected signature of function. If an indirect call is executed with an index that points to a function with signature different of what is expected by this indirect call, this trap is raised.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.OutOfFuel)

### OutOfFuel = 9

This trap is raised when a WebAssembly execution ran out of fuel.

The Wasmi execution engine can be configured to instrument its internal bytecode so that fuel is consumed for each executed instruction. This is useful to deterministically halt or yield a WebAssembly execution.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.GrowthOperationLimited)

### GrowthOperationLimited = 10

This trap is raised when a growth operation was attempted and an
installed `wasmi::ResourceLimiter` returned `Err(...)` from the
associated `table_growing` or `memory_growing` method, indicating a
desire on the part of the embedder to trap the interpreter rather than
merely fail the growth operation.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

    fn [decode_untyped_slice](https://docs.rs#tymethod.decode_untyped_slice)(params: &[[UntypedVal](https://docs.rs/struct.UntypedVal.html)]) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [UntypedError](https://docs.rs/enum.UntypedError.html)>;
}## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasmi_core/untyped.rs.html#416)#### fn [decode_untyped_slice](https://docs.rs#tymethod.decode_untyped_slice)(params: &[[UntypedVal](https://docs.rs/struct.UntypedVal.html)]) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [UntypedError](https://docs.rs/enum.UntypedError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wasmi_core/untyped.rs.html#416)

#### fn [decode_untyped_slice](https://docs.rs#tymethod.decode_untyped_slice)(params: &[[UntypedVal](https://docs.rs/struct.UntypedVal.html)]) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [UntypedError](https://docs.rs/enum.UntypedError.html)>

Decodes the slice of [ UntypedVal](https://docs.rs/struct.UntypedVal.html) as a value of type

`Self`.[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

`Self` can either be a single type or a tuple of types depending
on the length of the `slice`.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

If the tuple length of `Self` and the length of `slice` does not match.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

#### fn [encode_untyped_slice](https://docs.rs#tymethod.encode_untyped_slice)(
    self,
    results: &mut [[UntypedVal](https://docs.rs/struct.UntypedVal.html)],
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [UntypedError](https://docs.rs/enum.UntypedError.html)>

Encodes the slice of [ UntypedVal](https://docs.rs/struct.UntypedVal.html) from the given value of type

`Self`.[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

`Self` can either be a single type or a tuple of types depending
on the length of the `slice`.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

If the tuple length of `Self` and the length of `slice` does not match.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# HostError in wasmi_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasmi_core/1.1.0/wasmi_core/trait.HostError.html

## Expand description

Trait that allows the host to return custom error.

It should be useful for representing custom traps, troubles at instantiation time or other host specific conditions.

Types that implement this trait can automatically be converted to `wasmi::Error` and `wasmi::Trap`
and will be represented as a boxed `HostError`. You can then use the various methods on `wasmi::Error`
to get your custom error type back

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use std::fmt;
use wasmi_core::{Trap, HostError};
#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone)]
struct MyError {
    code: u32,
}
impl fmt::Display for MyError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "MyError, code={}", self.code)
    }
}
impl HostError for MyError { }
fn failable_fn() -> Result<(), Trap> {
    let my_error = MyError { code: 42 };
    // Note how you can just convert your errors to `wasmi::Error`
    Err(my_error.into())
}
// Get a reference to the concrete error
match failable_fn() {
    Err(trap) => {
        let my_error: &MyError = trap.downcast_ref().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(my_error.code, 42);
    }
    _ => panic!(),
}
// get the concrete error itself
match failable_fn() {
    Err(err) => {
        let my_error = match err.downcast_ref::<MyError>() {
            Some(host_error) => host_error.clone(),
            None => panic!("expected host error `MyError` but found: {}", err),
        };
        assert_eq!(my_error.code, 42);
    }
    _ => panic!(),
}
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# wasmi_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasmi_core/latest/wasmi_core/

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [hint](https://docs.rs/hint/index.html)
- [simd](https://docs.rs/simd/index.html)
- Defines the entire Wasm `simd`proposal API.
- [wasm](https://docs.rs/wasm/index.html)
- Execution helpers for Wasm or Wasmi instructions.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Element](https://docs.rs/struct.ElementSegment.html)- Segment
- A Wasm `ElementSegment`
- [Element](https://docs.rs/struct.ElementSegmentRef.html)- Segment - Ref
- A shared reference to a Wasm `ElementSegment`
- [F32](https://docs.rs/struct.F32.html)
- A 32-bit `f32`type.
- [F64](https://docs.rs/struct.F64.html)
- A 64-bit `f64`type.
- [Fuel](https://docs.rs/struct.Fuel.html)
- The remaining and consumed fuel counters.
- [Fuel](https://docs.rs/struct.FuelCostsProvider.html)- Costs - Provider
- Type storing all kinds of fuel costs of instructions.
- [Func](https://docs.rs/struct.FuncType.html)- Type
- A function type representing a function’s parameter and result types.
- [Global](https://docs.rs/struct.Global.html)
- A global variable entity.
- [Global](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobalType.html)- Type
- The type of a global variable.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.Memory.html)
- A Wasm linear memory.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryType.html)- Type
- The memory type of a linear memory.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryTypeBuilder.html)- Type - Builder
- A builder for `MemoryType`
- [Resource](https://docs.rs/struct.ResourceLimiterRef.html)- Limiter - Ref
- Wrapper around an optional `&mut dyn``ResourceLimiter`
- [Table](https://docs.rs/struct.Table.html)
- A Wasm table entity.
- [Table](https://docs.rs/struct.TableType.html)- Type
- A Wasm table descriptor.
- [Trap](https://docs.rs/struct.Trap.html)
- Error type which can be returned by Wasm code or by the host environment.
- [Typed](https://docs.rs/struct.TypedVal.html)- Val
- An `UntypedVal``ValType`
- [Untyped](https://docs.rs/struct.UntypedVal.html)- Val
- An untyped value.
- [V128](https://docs.rs/struct.V128.html)
- The Wasm `simd`proposal’s`v128`type.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Fuel](https://docs.rs/enum.FuelError.html)- Error
- An error that may be encountered when using `Fuel`
- [Func](https://docs.rs/enum.FuncTypeError.html)- Type - Error
- Errors that can occur upon type checking function signatures.
- [Global](https://docs.rs/enum.GlobalError.html)- Error
- An error that may occur upon operating on global variables.
- [Index](https://docs.rs/enum.IndexType.html)- Type
- The index type used for addressing memories and tables.
- [Limiter](https://docs.rs/enum.LimiterError.html)- Error
- An error either returned by a `ResourceLimiter`
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/enum.MemoryError.html)- Error
- An error that may occur upon operating with virtual or linear memory.
- [Mutability](https://docs.rs/enum.Mutability.html)
- The mutability of a global variable.
- [Table](https://docs.rs/enum.TableError.html)- Error
- Errors that may occur upon operating with table entities.
- [Trap](https://docs.rs/enum.TrapCode.html)- Code
- Error type which can be thrown by wasm code or by host environment.
- [Untyped](https://docs.rs/enum.UntypedError.html)- Error
- An error that may occur upon encoding or decoding slices of `UntypedVal`
- [ValType](https://docs.rs/enum.ValType.html)
- Type of a value.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Decode](https://docs.rs/trait.DecodeUntypedSlice.html)- Untyped - Slice
- Tuple types that allow to decode a slice of `UntypedVal`
- [Encode](https://docs.rs/trait.EncodeUntypedSlice.html)- Untyped - Slice
- Tuple types that allow to encode a slice of `UntypedVal`
- [Fuel](https://docs.rs/trait.FuelCosts.html)- Costs
- Fuel costs for Wasmi IR instructions.
- [Host](https://docs.rs/trait.HostError.html)- Error
- Trait that allows the host to return custom error.
- [ReadAs](https://docs.rs/trait.ReadAs.html)
- Implemented by types that can be read (or decoded) as `T`.
- [Resource](https://docs.rs/trait.ResourceLimiter.html)- Limiter
- Used by hosts to limit resource consumption of instances.
- [Typed](https://docs.rs/trait.Typed.html)
- Types that are associated to a static Wasm type.
- [WriteAs](https://docs.rs/trait.WriteAs.html)
- Implemented by types that can be written to (or encoded) as `T`.

# wasmi_core 1.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wasmi_core/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# libm 0.2.16 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/libm/^0.2.11

`libm`

A Rust implementations of the C math library.

## Usage

`libm` provides fallback implementations for Rust's [float math functions](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.f32.html) in
`core`, and the [ core_float_math](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/137578) feature. If what is available suits your
needs, there is no need to add

`libm` as a dependency.If more functionality is needed, this crate can also be used directly:

```
[]
 = "0.2.11"
```

Please check [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/CONTRIBUTING.md)

This crate supports rustc 1.63 and newer.

# wasmi_core 2.0.0-beta.4 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wasmi_core/2.0.0-beta.4

| Continuous Integration | Test Coverage | Documentation | Crates.io |
|---|---|---|---|

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

## Distinct Features

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Efficient and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for `no_std`embedded environments
- Compiler/JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/)to act as drop-in replacement.
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Security Audits

Wasmi is suitable for safety critical use cases and has been audited twice.

| Wasmi Version(s) | Auditor | Contractor | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.36.0`-`0.38.0` | [Runtime Verification Inc.](https://runtimeverification.com/) | [Stellar Development Foundation](https://stellar.org/foundation) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2024-11-27.pdf) |
| `0.31.0` | [SRLabs](https://www.srlabs.de/) | [Parity Technologies](https://www.parity.io/) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2023-12-20.pdf) |

## Docs

- 📖 [Usage Guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md): learn how to use the[Wasmi API](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi)properly.
- 🛠️ [Development Guide](https://docs.rs/docs/developement.md): learn how to develop for Wasmi.
- ✨ [Crate Features](https://docs.rs/wasmi/latest/wasmi/#crate-features): learn about`wasmi`crate features.

## WebAssembly Features

| WebAssembly Proposal | WebAssembly Proposal | |||||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ | `mutable-global` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `custom-page-sizes` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1197)`0.41.0` | |
| ✅ | `saturating-float-to-int` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `memory64` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1357)`0.41.0` | |
| ✅ | `sign-extension` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `wide-arithmetic` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1369)`0.42.0` | |
| ✅ | `multi-value` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1364)`0.43.0` | |
| ✅ | `bulk-memory` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628)`0.24.0` | ✅ | `relaxed-simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/1443)`0.44.0` | |
| ✅ | `reference-types` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/635)`0.24.0` | 📅 | `function-references` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) | |
| ✅ | `tail-calls` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/683)`0.28.0` | 📅 | `gc` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) | |
| ✅ | `extended-const` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707)`0.29.0` | 📅 | `threads` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) | |
| ✅ | `multi-memory` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1191)`0.37.0` | 📅 | `exception-handling` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |

| Embeddings | ||
|---|---|---|
| ✅ | [WASI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI) | WASI ( `wasip1`) support via the.`wasmi_wasi`crate |
| ✅ | [C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api) | Official Wasm C-API support via the .`wasmi_c_api_impl`crate |

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

## Distinct Features

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Efficient and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for `no_std`embedded environments
- Compiler/JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/)to act as drop-in replacement.
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Security Audits

Wasmi is suitable for safety critical use cases and has been audited twice.

| Wasmi Version(s) | Auditor | Contractor | Report |

| WebAssembly Proposal | WebAssembly Proposal | |||||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

# wasmi_core 2.0.0-beta.0 - Docs.rs

| Continuous Integration | Test Coverage | Documentation | Crates.io |
|---|---|---|---|

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

## Distinct Features

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Efficient and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for `no_std`embedded environments
- Compiler/JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/)to act as drop-in replacement.
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Security Audits

Wasmi is suitable for safety critical use cases and has been audited twice.

| Wasmi Version(s) | Auditor | Contractor | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.36.0`-`0.38.0` | [Runtime Verification Inc.](https://runtimeverification.com/) | [Stellar Development Foundation](https://stellar.org/foundation) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2024-11-27.pdf) |
| `0.31.0` | [SRLabs](https://www.srlabs.de/) | [Parity Technologies](https://www.parity.io/) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2023-12-20.pdf) |

## Docs

- 📖 [Usage Guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md): learn how to use the[Wasmi API](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi)properly.
- 🛠️ [Development Guide](https://docs.rs/docs/developement.md): learn how to develop for Wasmi.
- ✨ [Crate Features](https://docs.rs/wasmi/latest/wasmi/#crate-features): learn about`wasmi`crate features.

## WebAssembly Features

| ✅ | `sign-extension` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `wide-arithmetic` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1369)`0.42.0` | |
| ✅ | `multi-value` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1364)`0.43.0` | |

| Continuous Integration | Test Coverage | Documentation | Crates.io |
|---|---|---|---|

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

## Distinct Features

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Efficient and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for `no_std`embedded environments
- Compiler/JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/)to act as drop-in replacement.
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Security Audits

Wasmi is suitable for safety critical use cases and has been audited twice.

| Wasmi Version(s) | Auditor | Contractor | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.36.0`-`0.38.0` | [Runtime Verification Inc.](https://runtimeverification.com/) | [Stellar Development Foundation](https://stellar.org/foundation) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2024-11-27.pdf) |
| `0.31.0` | [SRLabs](https://www.srlabs.de/) | [Parity Technologies](https://www.parity.io/) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2023-12-20.pdf) |

## Docs

- 📖 [Usage Guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md): learn how to use the[Wasmi API](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi)properly.
- 🛠️ [Development Guide](https://docs.rs/docs/developement.md): learn how to develop for Wasmi.
- ✨ [Crate Features](https://docs.rs/wasmi/latest/wasmi/#crate-features): learn about`wasmi`crate features.

## WebAssembly Features

| ✅ | `sign-extension` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `wide-arithmetic` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1369)`0.42.0` | |
| ✅ | `multi-value` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1364)`0.43.0` | |

# wasmi_core 1.0.0 - Docs.rs

| Continuous Integration | Test Coverage | Documentation | Crates.io |
|---|---|---|---|

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

## Distinct Features

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Efficient and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for `no_std`embedded environments
- Compiler/JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/)to act as drop-in replacement.
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Security Audits

Wasmi is suitable for safety critical use cases and has been audited twice.

| Wasmi Version(s) | Auditor | Contractor | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.36.0`-`0.38.0` | [Runtime Verification Inc.](https://runtimeverification.com/) | [Stellar Development Foundation](https://stellar.org/foundation) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2024-11-27.pdf) |
| `0.31.0` | [SRLabs](https://www.srlabs.de/) | [Parity Technologies](https://www.parity.io/) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2023-12-20.pdf) |

## Docs

- 📖 [Usage Guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md): learn how to use the[Wasmi API](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi)properly.
- 🛠️ [Development Guide](https://docs.rs/docs/developement.md): learn how to develop for Wasmi.
- ✨ [Crate Features](https://docs.rs/wasmi/latest/wasmi/#crate-features): learn about`wasmi`crate features.

## WebAssembly Features

| ✅ | `saturating-float-to-int` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `memory64` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1357)`0.41.0` | |
| ✅ | `sign-extension` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `wide-arithmetic` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1369)`0.42.0` | |
| ✅ | `multi-value` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1364)`0.43.0` | |
| ✅ | `bulk-memory` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628)`0.24.0` | ✅ | `relaxed-simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/1443)`0.44.0` | |

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

## Distinct Features

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Efficient and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for `no_std`embedded environments
- Compiler/JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/)to act as drop-in replacement.
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Security Audits

Wasmi is suitable for safety critical use cases and has been audited twice.

| Wasmi Version(s) | Auditor | Contractor | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.36.0`-`0.38.0` | [Runtime Verification Inc.](https://runtimeverification.com/) | [Stellar Development Foundation](https://stellar.org/foundation) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2024-11-27.pdf) |
| `0.31.0` | [SRLabs](https://www.srlabs.de/) | [Parity Technologies](https://www.parity.io/) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2023-12-20.pdf) |

## Docs

- 📖 [Usage Guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md): learn how to use the[Wasmi API](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi)properly.
- 🛠️ [Development Guide](https://docs.rs/docs/developement.md): learn how to develop for Wasmi.
- ✨ [Crate Features](https://docs.rs/wasmi/latest/wasmi/#crate-features): learn about`wasmi`crate features.

## Security Audits

| Wasmi Version(s) | Auditor | Contractor | Report |

## Distinct Features

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Low-overhead and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for embedded environments.
- Compiler/JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/).

- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

# wasmi_core 0.47.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wasmi_core/0.47.2

| Continuous Integration | Test Coverage | Documentation | Crates.io |
|---|---|---|---|

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

## Security Audits

Wasmi is suitable for safety critical use cases and has been audited several times already.

| Wasmi Version(s) | Auditor | Contractor | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.36.0`-`0.38.0` | [Runtime Verification Inc.](https://runtimeverification.com/) | [Stellar Development Foundation](https://stellar.org/foundation) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2024-11-27.pdf) |
| `0.31.0` | [SRLabs](https://www.srlabs.de/) | [Parity Technologies](https://www.parity.io/) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2023-12-20.pdf) |

## Distinct Features

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Low-overhead and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for embedded environments.
- JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/).
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Usage

Refer to the [Wasmi usage guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md) to learn how properly to use [Wasmi](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi).

## WebAssembly Features

| WebAssembly Proposal | WebAssembly Proposal | |||||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ | `mutable-global` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `custom-page-sizes` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1197)`0.41.0` | |
| ✅ | `saturating-float-to-int` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `memory64` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1357)`0.41.0` | |
| ✅ | `sign-extension` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `wide-arithmetic` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1369)`0.42.0` | |
| ✅ | `multi-value` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1364)`0.43.0` | |
| ✅ | `bulk-memory` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628)`0.24.0` | ✅ | `relaxed-simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/1443)`0.44.0` | |
| ✅ | `reference-types` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/635)`0.24.0` | 📅 | `function-references` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) | |
| ✅ | `tail-calls` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/683)`0.28.0` | 📅 | `gc` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) | |
| ✅ | `extended-const` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707)`0.29.0` | 📅 | `threads` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) | |
| ✅ | `multi-memory` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1191)`0.37.0` | 📅 | `exception-handling` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |

| Embeddings | ||
|---|---|---|
| ✅ | [WASI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI) | WASI ( `wasip1`) support via the.`wasmi_wasi`crate |
| ✅ | [C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api) | Official Wasm C-API support via the .`wasmi_c_api_impl`crate |

## Crate Features

| Feature | Crates | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `std` | `wasmi``wasmi_core``wasmi_ir``wasmi_collections` | Enables usage of Rust's standard library. This may have some performance advantages when enabled. Disabling this feature makes Wasmi compile on platforms that do not provide Rust's standard library such as many embedded platforms. Enabled by default. |
| `wat` | `wasmi` | Enables support to parse Wat encoded Wasm modules. Enabled by default. |
| `simd` | `wasmi``wasmi_core``wasmi_ir``wasmi_cli` | Enables support for the Wasm `simd`and`relaxed-simd`proposals. Note that this may introduce execution overhead and increased memory consumption for Wasm executions that do not need Wasm`simd`functionality.  Disabled by default. |
| `hash-collections` | `wasmi``wasmi_collections` | Enables use of hash-map based collections in Wasmi internals. This might yield performance improvements in some use cases. Disabled by default. |
| `prefer-btree-collections` | `wasmi``wasmi_collections` | Enforces use of btree-map based collections in Wasmi internals. This may yield performance improvements and memory consumption decreases in some use cases. Also it enables Wasmi to run on platforms that have no random source. Disabled by default. |
| `extra-checks` | `wasmi` | Enables extra runtime checks in the Wasmi executor. Expected execution overhead is ~20%. Enable this if your focus is on safety. Disable this for maximum execution performance. Disabled by default. |

## Development

### Build & Test

Clone the Wasmi repository and build using `cargo`:

```
git clone https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi.git --recursive
cd wasmi
cargo build
cargo test
```
### Benchmarks

In order to benchmark Wasmi use the following command:

```
cargo bench
```
Use `translate`, `instantiate`, `execute` or `overhead` filters to only run benchmarks that test performance of Wasm translation, instantiation, execution or miscellaneous overhead respectively, e.g. `cargo bench execute`.

## Supported Platforms

Wasmi supports a wide variety of architectures and platforms.

- Fore more details see this [list of supported platforms for Rust](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustc/platform-support.html).
- **Note:**Wasmi can be used in- `no_std`embedded environments, thus not requiring the standard library (- `std`).
- Only some platforms are checked in CI and guaranteed to be fully working by the Wasmi maintainers.

| ✅ | `sign-extension` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `wide-arithmetic` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1369)`0.42.0` | |
| ✅ | `multi-value` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1364)`0.43.0` | |
| ✅ | `bulk-memory` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628)`0.24.0` | ✅ | `relaxed-simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/1443)`0.44.0` | |
| ✅ | `reference-types` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/635)`0.24.0` | 📅 | `function-references` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) | |
| ✅ | `tail-calls` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/683)`0.28.0` | 📅 | `gc` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) | |
| ✅ | `extended-const` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707)`0.29.0` | 📅 | `threads` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) | |
| ✅ | `multi-memory` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1191)`0.37.0` | 📅 | `exception-handling` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |

| Embeddings | ||
|---|---|---|
| ✅ | [WASI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI) | WASI ( `wasip1`) support via the.`wasmi_wasi`crate |
| ✅ | [C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api) | Official Wasm C-API support via the .`wasmi_c_api_impl`crate |

## Crate Features

| Feature | Crates | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `std` | `wasmi``wasmi_core``wasmi_ir``wasmi_collections` | Enables usage of Rust's standard library. This may have some performance advantages when enabled. Disabling this feature makes Wasmi compile on platforms that do not provide Rust's standard library such as many embedded platforms. Enabled by default. |
| `wat` | `wasmi` | Enables support to parse Wat encoded Wasm modules. Enabled by default. |
| `simd` | `wasmi``wasmi_core``wasmi_ir``wasmi_cli` | Enables support for the Wasm `simd`and`relaxed-simd`proposals. Note that this may introduce execution overhead and increased memory consumption for Wasm executions that do not need Wasm`simd`functionality.  Disabled by default. |
| `hash-collections` | `wasmi``wasmi_collections` | Enables use of hash-map based collections in Wasmi internals. This might yield performance improvements in some use cases. Disabled by default. |
| `prefer-btree-collections` | `wasmi``wasmi_collections` | Enforces use of btree-map based collections in Wasmi internals. This may yield performance improvements and memory consumption decreases in some use cases. Also it enables Wasmi to run on platforms that have no random source. Disabled by default. |
| `extra-checks` | `wasmi` | Enables extra runtime checks in the Wasmi executor. Expected execution overhead is ~20%. Enable this if your focus is on safety. Disable this for maximum execution performance. Disabled by default. |

## Development

### Build & Test

Clone the Wasmi repository and build using `cargo`:

```
git clone https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi.git --recursive
cd wasmi
cargo build
cargo test
```
### Benchmarks

In order to benchmark Wasmi use the following command:

```
cargo bench
```
Use `translate`, `instantiate`, `execute` or `overhead` filters to only run benchmarks that test performance of Wasm translation, instantiation, execution or miscellaneous overhead respectively, e.g. `cargo bench execute`.

## Supported Platforms

Wasmi supports a wide variety of architectures and platforms.

- Fore more details see this [list of supported platforms for Rust](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustc/platform-support.html).
- **Note:**Wasmi can be used in- `no_std`embedded environments, thus not requiring the standard library (- `std`).
- Only some platforms are checked in CI and guaranteed to be fully working by the Wasmi maintainers.

|---|---|---|---|

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

## Security Audits

Wasmi is suitable for safety critical use cases and has been audited several times already.

| Wasmi Version(s) | Auditor | Contractor | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.36.0`-`0.38.0` | [Runtime Verification Inc.](https://runtimeverification.com/) | [Stellar Development Foundation](https://stellar.org/foundation) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2024-11-27.pdf) |
| `0.31.0` | [SRLabs](https://www.srlabs.de/) | [Parity Technologies](https://www.parity.io/) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2023-12-20.pdf) |

## Distinct Features

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Low-overhead and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for embedded environments.
- JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/).
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Usage

Refer to the [Wasmi usage guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md) to learn how properly to use [Wasmi](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi).

## WebAssembly Features

| WebAssembly Proposal | WebAssembly Proposal | |||||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ | `mutable-global` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `custom-page-sizes` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1197)`0.41.0` | |
| ✅ | `saturating-float-to-int` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `memory64` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1357)`0.41.0` | |
| ✅ | `sign-extension` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `wide-arithmetic` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1369)`0.42.0` | |
| ✅ | `multi-value` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1364)`0.43.0` | |
| ✅ | `bulk-memory` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628)`0.24.0` | ✅ | `relaxed-simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/1443)`0.44.0` | |
| ✅ | `reference-types` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/635)`0.24.0` | 📅 | `function-references` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) | |
| ✅ | `tail-calls` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/683)`0.28.0` | 📅 | `gc` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) | |
| ✅ | `extended-const` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707)`0.29.0` | 📅 | `threads` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) | |
| ✅ | `multi-memory` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1191)`0.37.0` | 📅 | `exception-handling` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |

| Embeddings | ||

| Feature | Crates | Description |
|---|---|---|

Disabling this feature makes Wasmi compile on platforms that do not provide Rust's standard library such as many embedded platforms. Enabled by default. |
| `wat` | `wasmi` | Enables support to parse Wat encoded Wasm modules. Enabled by default. |
| `simd` | `wasmi``wasmi_core``wasmi_ir``wasmi_cli` | Enables support for the Wasm `simd`and`relaxed-simd`proposals. Note that this may introduce execution overhead and increased memory consumption for Wasm executions that do not need Wasm`simd`functionality.  Disabled by default. |
| `hash-collections` | `wasmi``wasmi_collections` | Enables use of hash-map based collections in Wasmi internals. This might yield performance improvements in some use cases. Disabled by default. |
| `prefer-btree-collections` | `wasmi``wasmi_collections` | Enforces use of btree-map based collections in Wasmi internals. This may yield performance improvements and memory consumption decreases in some use cases. Also it enables Wasmi to run on platforms that have no random source. Disabled by default. |
| `extra-checks` | `wasmi` | Enables extra runtime checks in the Wasmi executor. Expected execution overhead is ~20%. Enable this if your focus is on safety. Disable this for maximum execution performance. Disabled by default. |

|---|---|---|---|
| `0.36.0`-`0.38.0` | [Runtime Verification Inc.](https://runtimeverification.com/) | [Stellar Development Foundation](https://stellar.org/foundation) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2024-11-27.pdf) |
| `0.31.0` | [SRLabs](https://www.srlabs.de/) | [Parity Technologies](https://www.parity.io/) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2023-12-20.pdf) |

## Distinct Features

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Low-overhead and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for embedded environments.
- JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/).
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Usage

Refer to the [Wasmi usage guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md) to learn how properly to use [Wasmi](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi).

## WebAssembly Features

| WebAssembly Proposal | WebAssembly Proposal | |||||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ | `mutable-global` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `custom-page-sizes` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1197)`0.41.0` | |
| ✅ | `saturating-float-to-int` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `memory64` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1357)`0.41.0` | |
| ✅ | `sign-extension` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `wide-arithmetic` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1369)`0.42.0` | |
| ✅ | `multi-value` | ≥ `0.14.0` | ✅ | `simd` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1364)`0.43.0` | |
| ✅ | `bulk-memory` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628)`0.24.0` | 📅 | `relaxed-simd` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1431) | |
| ✅ | `reference-types` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/635)`0.24.0` | 📅 | `function-references` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) | |
| ✅ | `tail-calls` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/683)`0.28.0` | 📅 | `gc` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) | |
| ✅ | `extended-const` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707)`0.29.0` | 📅 | `threads` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) | |
| ✅ | `multi-memory` | [≥ ](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1191)`0.37.0` | 📅 | `exception-handling` | [Tracking Issue](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |

| Embeddings | ||
|---|---|---|
| ✅ | [WASI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI) | WASI ( `wasip1`) support via the.`wasmi_wasi`crate |
| ✅ | [C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api) | Official Wasm C-API support via the .`wasmi_c_api_impl`crate |

## Crate Features

| Feature | Crates | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `std` | `wasmi``wasmi_core``wasmi_ir``wasmi_collections` | Enables usage of Rust's standard library. This may have some performance advantages when enabled. Disabling this feature makes Wasmi compile on platforms that do not provide Rust's standard library such as many embedded platforms. Enabled by default. |
| `wat` | `wasmi` | Enables support to parse Wat encoded Wasm modules. Enabled by default. |
| `simd` | `wasmi``wasmi_core``wasmi_ir``wasmi_cli` | Enables support for the Wasm `simd`proposal. Note that this may introduce execution overhead and increased memory consumption for Wasm executions that do not need Wasm`simd`functionality.  Disabled by default. |
| `hash-collections` | `wasmi``wasmi_collections` | Enables use of hash-map based collections in Wasmi internals. This might yield performance improvements in some use cases. Disabled by default. |
| `prefer-btree-collections` | `wasmi``wasmi_collections` | Enforces use of btree-map based collections in Wasmi internals. This may yield performance improvements and memory consumption decreases in some use cases. Also it enables Wasmi to run on platforms that have no random source. Disabled by default. |
| `extra-checks` | `wasmi` | Enables extra runtime checks in the Wasmi executor. Expected execution overhead is ~20%. Enable this if your focus is on safety. Disable this for maximum execution performance. Disabled by default. |

## Development

### Build & Test

Clone the Wasmi repository and build using `cargo`:

```
git clone https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi.git --recursive
cd wasmi
cargo build
cargo test
```
### Benchmarks

In order to benchmark Wasmi use the following command:

```
cargo bench
```
Use `translate`, `instantiate`, `execute` or `overhead` filters to only run benchmarks that test performance of Wasm translation, instantiation, execution or miscellaneous overhead respectively, e.g. `cargo bench execute`.

## Supported Platforms

Wasmi supports a wide variety of architectures and platforms.

- Fore more details see this [list of supported platforms for Rust](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustc/platform-support.html).
- **Note:**Wasmi can be used in- `no_std`embedded environments, thus not requiring the standard library (- `std`).
- Only some platforms are checked in CI and guaranteed to be fully working by the Wasmi maintainers.

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

## Security Audits

Wasmi is suitable for safety critical use cases and has been audited several times already.

| Wasmi Version(s) | Auditor | Contractor | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.36.0`-`0.38.0` | [Runtime Verification Inc.](https://runtimeverification.com/) | [Stellar Development Foundation](https://stellar.org/foundation) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2024-11-27.pdf) |
| `0.31.0` | [SRLabs](https://www.srlabs.de/) | [Parity Technologies](https://www.parity.io/) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2023-12-20.pdf) |

## Distinct Features

The following list states some of the distinct features of Wasmi.

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Low-overhead and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for embedded environments.
- JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/).
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Usage

Refer to the [Wasmi usage guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md) to learn how properly to use [Wasmi](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi).

## WebAssembly Proposals

The new Wasmi engine supports a variety of WebAssembly proposals and will support even more of them in the future.

| WebAssembly Proposal | Status | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| `mutable-global` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0` |
| `saturating-float-to-int` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0` |
| `sign-extension` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0` |
| `multi-value` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0` |
| `bulk-memory` | ✅ | ≥ `0.24.0`[(#628)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628) |
| `reference-types` | ✅ | ≥ `0.24.0`[(#635)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/635) |
| `tail-calls` | ✅ | ≥ `0.28.0`[(#683)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/683) |
| `extended-const` | ✅ | ≥ `0.29.0`[(#707)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707) |
| `multi-memory` | ✅ | ≥ `0.37.0`[(#1191)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1191) |
| `custom-page-sizes` | ✅ | ≥ `0.41.0`[(#1197)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1197) |
| `memory64` | ✅ | ≥ `0.41.0`[(#1357)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1357) |
| `wide-arithmetic` | ✅ | ≥ `0.42.0`[(#1369)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1369) |
| `simd` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#1364)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1364) |
| `relaxed-simd` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. Depends on `simd`. |
| `function-references` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#774)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) |
| `gc` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#775)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) |
| `threads` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#777)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) |
| `exception-handling` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#1037)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |
| [WASI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for WASI ( `wasip1`) via the.`wasmi_wasi`crate |
| [C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for the official Wasm C-API via the .`wasmi_c_api_impl`crate |

| `extended-const` | ✅ | ≥ `0.29.0`[(#707)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707) |
| `multi-memory` | ✅ | ≥ `0.37.0`[(#1191)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1191) |
| `custom-page-sizes` | ✅ | ≥ `0.41.0`[(#1197)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1197) |
| `memory64` | ✅ | ≥ `0.41.0`[(#1357)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1357) |
| `simd` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#1364)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1364) |
| `relaxed-simd` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. Depends on `simd`. |
| `function-references` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#774)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) |
| `gc` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#775)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) |
| `threads` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#777)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) |
| `exception-handling` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#1037)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |
| `wide-arithmetic` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#1369)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1369) |
| [WASI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for WASI ( `wasip1`) via the.`wasmi_wasi`crate |
| [C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for the official Wasm C-API via the .`wasmi_c_api_impl`crate |

## Development

### Build & Test

Clone the Wasmi repository and build using `cargo`:

```
git clone https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi.git --recursive
cd wasmi
cargo build
cargo test
```
### Benchmarks

In order to benchmark Wasmi use the following command:

```
cargo bench
```
Use `translate`, `instantiate`, `execute` or `overhead` filters to only run benchmarks that test performance of Wasm translation, instantiation, execution or miscellaneous overhead respectively, e.g. `cargo bench execute`.

## Supported Platforms

Wasmi supports a wide variety of architectures and platforms.

- Fore more details see this [list of supported platforms for Rust](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustc/platform-support.html).
- **Note:**Wasmi can be used in- `no_std`embedded environments, thus not requiring the standard library (- `std`).
- Only some platforms are checked in CI and guaranteed to be fully working by the Wasmi maintainers.

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

## Security Audits

Wasmi is suitable for safety critical use cases and has been audited several times already.

| Wasmi Version(s) | Auditor | Contractor | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.36.0`-`0.38.0` | [Runtime Verification Inc.](https://runtimeverification.com/) | [Stellar Development Foundation](https://stellar.org/foundation) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2024-11-27.pdf) |
| `0.31.0` | [SRLabs](https://www.srlabs.de/) | [Parity Technologies](https://www.parity.io/) | [PDF](https://docs.rs/resources/audit-2023-12-20.pdf) |

## Distinct Features

The following list states some of the distinct features of Wasmi.

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Low-overhead and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for embedded environments.
- JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/).
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Usage

Refer to the [Wasmi usage guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md) to learn how properly to use [Wasmi](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi).

## WebAssembly Proposals

The new Wasmi engine supports a variety of WebAssembly proposals and will support even more of them in the future.

| WebAssembly Proposal | Status | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| `mutable-global` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0` |
| `saturating-float-to-int` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0` |
| `sign-extension` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0` |
| `multi-value` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0` |
| `bulk-memory` | ✅ | ≥ `0.24.0`[(#628)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628) |
| `reference-types` | ✅ | ≥ `0.24.0`[(#635)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/635) |
| `tail-calls` | ✅ | ≥ `0.28.0`[(#683)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/683) |
| `extended-const` | ✅ | ≥ `0.29.0`[(#707)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707) |
| `multi-memory` | ✅ | ≥ `0.37.0`[(#1191)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1191) |
| `custom-page-sizes` | ✅ | ≥ `0.41.0`[(#1197)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1197) |
| `memory64` | ✅ | ≥ `0.41.0`[(#1357)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1357) |
| `simd` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#1364)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1364) |
| `relaxed-simd` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. Depends on `simd`. |
| `function-references` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#774)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) |
| `gc` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#775)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) |
| `threads` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#777)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) |
| `exception-handling` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#1037)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |
| `wide-arithmetic` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#1369)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1369) |
| [WASI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for WASI ( `wasip1`) via the.`wasmi_wasi`crate |
| [C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for the official Wasm C-API via the .`wasmi_c_api_impl`crate |

| `saturating-float-to-int` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0`. |
| `sign-extension` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0`. |
| `multi-value` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0`. |
| `bulk-memory` | ✅ | ≥ `0.24.0`.[(#628)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628) |
| `reference-types` | ✅ | ≥ `0.24.0`.[(#635)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/635) |
| `tail-calls` | ✅ | ≥ `0.28.0`.[(#683)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/683) |
| `extended-const` | ✅ | ≥ `0.29.0`.[(#707)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707) |
| `multi-memory` | ✅ | ≥ `0.37.0`.[(#1191)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1191) |
| `simd` | ❌ | Unlikely to be supported. |
| `relaxed-simd` | ❌ | Unlikely to be supported. Depends on `simd`. |
| `function-references` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#774)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) |
| `gc` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#775)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) |
| `threads` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#777)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) |
| `exception-handling` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#1037)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |
| `custom-page-sizes` | 📅 | Not yet implemented. [(#1197)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1197) |
| [WASI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for WASI ( `wasip1`) via the.`wasmi_wasi`crate |
| [C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for the official Wasm C-API via the .`wasmi_c_api_impl`crate |

## Development

### Build & Test

Clone the Wasmi repository and build using `cargo`:

```
git clone https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi.git --recursive
cd wasmi
cargo build
cargo test
```
### Benchmarks

In order to benchmark Wasmi use the following command:

```
cargo bench
```
Use `translate`, `instantiate`, `execute` or `overhead` filters to only run benchmarks that test performance of Wasm translation, instantiation, execution or miscellaneous overhead respectively, e.g. `cargo bench execute`.

## Supported Platforms

Wasmi supports a wide variety of architectures and platforms.

- Fore more details see this [list of supported platforms for Rust](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustc/platform-support.html).
- **Note:**Wasmi can be used in- `no_std`embedded environments, thus not requiring the standard library (- `std`).
- Only some platforms are checked in CI and guaranteed to be fully working by the Wasmi maintainers.

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

Version `0.31.0` has been [audited by SRLabs](https://docs.rs/resources/security-audit-2023-12-20.pdf).

## Distinct Features

The following list states some of the distinct features of Wasmi.

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Low-overhead and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for embedded environments.
- JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/).
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Usage

Refer to the [Wasmi usage guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md) to learn how properly to use [Wasmi](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi).

## WebAssembly Proposals

The new Wasmi engine supports a variety of WebAssembly proposals and will support even more of them in the future.

| WebAssembly Proposal | Status | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| `mutable-global` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0`. |
| `saturating-float-to-int` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0`. |
| `sign-extension` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0`. |
| `multi-value` | ✅ | ≥ `0.14.0`. |
| `bulk-memory` | ✅ | ≥ `0.24.0`.[(#628)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628) |
| `reference-types` | ✅ | ≥ `0.24.0`.[(#635)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/635) |
| `simd` | ❌ | Unlikely to be supported. |
| `tail-calls` | ✅ | ≥ `0.28.0`.[(#683)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/683) |
| `extended-const` | ✅ | ≥ `0.29.0`.[(#707)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707) |
| `multi-memory` | ✅ | ≥ `0.37.0`.[(#1191)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1191) |
| `function-references` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#774)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) |
| `gc` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#775)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) |
| `threads` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#777)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) |
| `relaxed-simd` | ❌ | Unlikely to be supported since `simd`is unlikely to be supported. |
| `component-model` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#897)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/897) |
| `exception-handling` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#1037)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |
| `branch-hinting` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#1036)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1136) |
| `custom-page-sizes` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#1197)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1197) |
| [WASI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for WASI ( `wasip1`) via the.`wasmi_wasi`crate |
| [C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for the official Wasm C-API via the .`wasmi_c_api_impl`crate |

## Development

### Build & Test

Clone the Wasmi repository and build using `cargo`:

```
git clone https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi.git --recursive
cd wasmi
cargo build
cargo test
```
### Benchmarks

In order to benchmark Wasmi use the following command:

```
cargo bench
```
Use `translate`, `instantiate`, `execute` or `overhead` filters to only run benchmarks that test performance of Wasm translation, instantiation, execution or miscellaneous overhead respectively, e.g. `cargo bench execute`.

We maintain a timeline for benchmarks of every commit to `master` that [can be viewed here](https://wasmi-labs.github.io/wasmi/benchmarks/).

## Supported Platforms

Wasmi supports a wide variety of architectures and platforms.

- Fore more details see this [list of supported platforms for Rust](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustc/platform-support.html).
- **Note:**Wasmi can be used in- `no_std`embedded environments, thus not requiring the standard library (- `std`).
- Only some platforms are checked in CI and guaranteed to be fully working by the Wasmi maintainers.

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

Version `0.31.0` has been [audited by SRLabs](https://docs.rs/resources/security-audit-2023-12-20.pdf).

## Announcement: Transfer of Ownership

As of 2024-02-01, the original owner and maintainer of the Wasmi project, Parity Technologies, has officially transferred ownership of the project to me, Robin Freyler. Read more about this transfer [here](https://docs.rs/NEWS.md#announcement-transfer-of-ownership).

## Distinct Features

The following list states some of the distinct features of Wasmi.

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Low-overhead and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for embedded environments.
- JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/).
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Usage

Refer to the [Wasmi usage guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md) to learn how properly to use [Wasmi](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi).

## WebAssembly Proposals

The new Wasmi engine supports a variety of WebAssembly proposals and will support even more of them in the future.

| WebAssembly Proposal | Status | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| `mutable-global` | ✅ | Since version `0.14.0`. |
| `saturating-float-to-int` | ✅ | Since version `0.14.0`. |
| `sign-extension` | ✅ | Since version `0.14.0`. |
| `multi-value` | ✅ | Since version `0.14.0`. |
| `bulk-memory` | ✅ | Since version `0.24.0`.[(#628)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628) |
| `reference-types` | ✅ | Since version `0.24.0`.[(#635)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/635) |
| `simd` | ❌ | Unlikely to be supported. |
| `tail-calls` | ✅ | Since version `0.28.0`.[(#683)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/683) |
| `extended-const` | ✅ | Since version `0.29.0`.[(#707)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707) |
| `function-references` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#774)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) |
| `gc` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#775)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) |
| `multi-memory` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#776)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/776) |
| `threads` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#777)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) |
| `relaxed-simd` | ❌ | Unlikely to be supported since `simd`is unlikely to be supported. |
| `component-model` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#897)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/897) |
| `exception-handling` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#1037)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |
| `branch-hinting` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#1036)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1136) |
| [WASI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for WASI ( `wasip1`) via the.`wasmi_wasi`crate |
| [C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for the official Wasm C-API via the .`wasmi_c_api_impl`crate |

## Development

### Build & Test

Clone the Wasmi repository and build using `cargo`:

```
git clone https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi.git --recursive
cd wasmi
cargo build
cargo test
```
### Benchmarks

In order to benchmark Wasmi use the following command:

```
cargo bench
```
Use `translate`, `instantiate`, `execute` or `overhead` filters to only run benchmarks that test performance of Wasm translation, instantiation, execution or miscellaneous overhead respectively, e.g. `cargo bench execute`.

We maintain a timeline for benchmarks of every commit to `master` that [can be viewed here](https://wasmi-labs.github.io/wasmi/benchmarks/).

## Supported Platforms

Wasmi supports a wide variety of architectures and platforms.

- Fore more details see this [list of supported platforms for Rust](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustc/platform-support.html).
- **Note:**Wasmi can be used in- `no_std`embedded environments, thus not requiring the standard library (- `std`).
- Only some platforms are checked in CI and guaranteed to be fully working by the Wasmi maintainers.

# wasmi_core 0.36.0 - Docs.rs

| Continuous Integration | Test Coverage | Documentation | Crates.io |
|---|---|---|---|

# Wasmi - WebAssembly (Wasm) Interpreter

Wasmi is an efficient and lightweight WebAssembly interpreter with a focus on constrained and embedded systems.

Version `0.31.0` has been [audited by SRLabs](https://docs.rs/resources/security-audit-2023-12-20.pdf).

## Announcement: Transfer of Ownership

As of 2024-02-01, the original owner and maintainer of the Wasmi project, Parity Technologies, has officially transferred ownership of the project to me, Robin Freyler. Read more about this transfer [here](https://docs.rs/NEWS.md#announcement-transfer-of-ownership).

## Distinct Features

The following list states some of the distinct features of Wasmi.

- Simple, correct and deterministic execution of WebAssembly.
- Low-overhead and cross-platform WebAssembly runtime for embedded environments.
- JIT bomb resisting translation.
- Loosely mirrors the [Wasmtime API](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/).
- 100% WebAssembly spec testsuite compliance.
- Built-in support for fuel metering.
- Supports the official [Wasm C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api).

## Usage

Refer to the [Wasmi usage guide](https://docs.rs/docs/usage.md) to learn how properly to use [Wasmi](https://crates.io/crates/wasmi).

## WebAssembly Proposals

The new Wasmi engine supports a variety of WebAssembly proposals and will support even more of them in the future.

| WebAssembly Proposal | Status | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| `mutable-global` | ✅ | Since version `0.14.0`. |
| `saturating-float-to-int` | ✅ | Since version `0.14.0`. |
| `sign-extension` | ✅ | Since version `0.14.0`. |
| `multi-value` | ✅ | Since version `0.14.0`. |
| `bulk-memory` | ✅ | Since version `0.24.0`.[(#628)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/628) |
| `reference-types` | ✅ | Since version `0.24.0`.[(#635)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/635) |
| `simd` | ❌ | Unlikely to be supported. |
| `tail-calls` | ✅ | Since version `0.28.0`.[(#683)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/683) |
| `extended-const` | ✅ | Since version `0.29.0`.[(#707)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/707) |
| `function-references` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#774)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/774) |
| `gc` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#775)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/775) |
| `multi-memory` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#776)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/776) |
| `threads` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#777)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/777) |
| `relaxed-simd` | ❌ | Unlikely to be supported since `simd`is unlikely to be supported. |
| `component-model` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#897)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/pull/897) |
| `exception-handling` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#1037)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1137) |
| `branch-hinting` | 📅 | Planned but not yet implemented. [(#1036)](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi/issues/1136) |
| [WASI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for WASI ( `wasip1`) via the.`wasmi_wasi`crate |
| [C-API](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasm-c-api) | 👨🔬 | Experimental support for the official Wasm C-API via the .`wasmi_c_api_impl`crate |

## Development

### Build & Test

Clone the Wasmi repository and build using `cargo`:

```
git clone https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi.git --recursive
cd wasmi
cargo build
cargo test
```
### Benchmarks

In order to benchmark Wasmi use the following command:

```
cargo bench
```
Use `translate`, `instantiate`, `execute` or `overhead` filters to only run benchmarks that test performance of Wasm translation, instantiation, execution or miscellaneous overhead respectively, e.g. `cargo bench execute`.

We maintain a timeline for benchmarks of every commit to `master` that [can be viewed here](https://wasmi-labs.github.io/wasmi/benchmarks/).

## Supported Platforms

Wasmi supports a wide variety of architectures and platforms.

- Fore more details see this [list of supported platforms for Rust](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustc/platform-support.html).
- **Note:**Wasmi can be used in- `no_std`embedded environments, thus not requiring the standard library (- `std`).
- Only some platforms are checked in CI and guaranteed to be fully working by the Wasmi maintainers.

Licensed under either of

- Apache License, Version 2.0, ([LICENSE-APACHE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-APACHE)or[http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0](http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0))
- MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT)or[http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT](http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT))

at your option.
